ideas.pitch: A lightweight B2B customer support widget for indie hackers that converts bug reports directly into paid feature requests.
ideas.title: RevDesk
ideas.why_it_could_win: RevHack focuses heavily on the Traction Run where teams must acquire real users or sales; this directly targets early-stage SaaS founders who are desperate to monetize user feedback.

ideas.pitch: A 1-click browser extension allowing student creators and newsletter writers to gate individual blog posts or assets for $0.10 via UPI/crypto.
ideas.title: MicroPayWall
ideas.why_it_could_win: It targets the BuildInPublic Award and the core theme of building something that can earn real money within the 7-day traction window following the 36-hour build.

ideas.pitch: An AI-powered resume review micro-SaaS with a built-in pay-what-you-want checkout that targets desperate engineering job seekers in India.
ideas.title: ResumeRoaster
ideas.why_it_could_win: It has an extremely clear go-to-market strategy for the post-hackathon traction week, making it trivial to spam college WhatsApp groups and secure first sales.

ideas.pitch: An instant digital menu generator for roadside food stalls and small cafes that creates an ordering webpage via a quick smartphone photo upload.
ideas.title: MenuGenie
ideas.why_it_could_win: Local offline businesses are the easiest market for student teams in India to land real paying customers during the 7-day traction run, fulfilling the ultimate RevHack metric.

ideas.pitch: A WhatsApp-first invoicing and payment reminder bot for Indian freelancers that automates payment follow-ups.
ideas.title: InvoicePulse
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages familiar communication channels (WhatsApp), ensuring high user engagement and making it easy to prove actual usage and traction to judges.
